results.answer: Two parts. (1) Consumable: succubus kiss is a timed drug that changes sheet numbers, so it belongs in the consumable-MODE lane, not the situational registry — ruling E case 2 (mode WITH real modifiers, +2 item to initiative and to saves vs emotion/mental, duration 10 minutes, survivesRest false, hidden from the Modes manager, activated by Use). It is currently absent from the 225 item-modes in core.json, so add it. (2) Initiative: do NOT add an 'initiative' target kind. There is no `initiative` StatRef, so a new kind could never be displayed, and the app's own convention is to put the bonus on the STATISTIC YOU ROLL for initiative with the word 'initiative' in the trigger — 36 shipped entries already do this. Use target `perception` with the exact incredible-initiative wording: when = "on initiative rolls (whatever statistic you roll for initiative — usually Perception)". A dedicated Initiative row on the sheet is a feature request for the backlog, not a blocking ruling.

results.why: This is not a rules question — the bonus and its trigger are unambiguous. It is a question about whether the sheet has any surface at all for a PURCHASED DOWNTIME SERVICE, and the codebase is currently contradictory rather than decided. Services are look-only catalog rows that are never added to inventory (AddItemsModal.tsx:162 'Reference only — services aren't added to your inventory'), and an item's situational entries only fire while it is equipped, worn or invested (explain.ts:180-182) — a hired informant is none of those. So the three canary entries already sitting in the registry can never fire, and any entry added for the four weekly tiers would be equally dead. Whether hired help deserves a place on the sheet is a product call about what the sheet is for, and a reasonable person could go either way.

options.label: No surface — leave downtime services unregistered (and retire the three dead canary entries)
options.looksLike: Buying a canary changes nothing on the sheet. Diplomacy shows no star. The service's description in the catalog is the whole of it, and the player remembers the +1 when they sit down to do downtime — exactly how the owner already ruled skill DCs and Potion of Disguise are handled.

options.label: Give services a surface — let a purchased service be marked ACTIVE, so its entry fires like a worn item
options.looksLike: Diplomacy gains a `*`; opening it shows 'Canary Tail — +1 circumstance to Gather Information about the individual you are having tailed'. Costs a new 'active' toggle for non-wearable purchases and a route for services into inventory, and puts a downtime-only note on a combat-facing sheet.

results.recommend: Option 1. It matches the owner's own precedent for downtime-and-DC-only bonuses ('there is a setting... the user will need to remember'), it needs no engine work, and it fixes a real defect for free by retiring three entries that silently do nothing. If option 1 is chosen, the other three canary-tail questions collapse with it.

results.answer: Cumulative, one line — and it needs no new mechanism. If these are registered at all (see the canary-tail-first-week decision), give week N the CUMULATIVE bonus (+1/+2/+3/+4) and give all four the BYTE-IDENTICAL `when` string. The shipped stacking rule then does the rest: poolSituationalLines keys on type + sign + normalised trigger and keeps only the highest, so a player holding weeks one and two sees a single '+2 circumstance', not '+1' and '+2'. Four separate stars would be the bug the cross-cutting ruling exists to prevent ("if i have +1 item bonus and a +2 item bonus it will only show the +2").

results.answer: Fold it, do not star it — and fix the affix bug that this exposes. Ruling B set the principle in one direction (a bonus the RULES restrict leaves passiveEffects and becomes a star); its converse holds here — in armour mode the +1 item bonus to Athletics has no printed restriction at all, so a star would promise a condition that does not exist and would leave the Athletics total wrong. The app knows the mode: attachments.ts identifies the host by itemType. Model it as an effectChoices/resolvedItemPassives pair keyed to the affixture (the energy-robe pattern), armour → passiveEffects.skills.athletics 1 + resistance, weapon → a situational strikeDamage entry (that one IS conditional: 'after you Activate the lodestone, until the end of your next turn'). BLOCKING BUG: affixing sets worn/equipped/invested all false (play.ts:747), and both derive.ts:705 and explain.ts:194 require one of those — so today an affixed spellheart contributes nothing at all, by either route. Treat an affixed item as in-use via its host, the same special case the etched-rune fix already makes.
results.evidence: DECISIONS.md §B (converse); src/rules/play.ts:747; src/rules/derive.ts:705-709; src/rules/explain.ts:194-203 (etched-rune special case); src/rules/attachments.ts:60-62; core.json items.energy-robe.effectChoices
